message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong that I didn't read a book to my son tonight because he has to go to school tomorrow. I'm a Christian, so I want to make sure my actions align with my faith. Let me break this down step by step. First, I know that as a parent, my role is to care for my child's well-being, both physically and spiritually. Reading to him is something I do regularly, and it's a bonding activity. It helps with his literacy skills and creates a routine that he probably looks forward to. So, not reading tonight might disrupt that routine. But why didn't I read to him tonight? Because he has school tomorrow. Maybe I thought he needed more sleep or rest. That makes sense because getting enough rest is important for his performance at school. As a Christian, I believe in taking care of the body because it's a temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). So, ensuring he's well-rested could be seen as fulfilling that responsibility. On the other hand, the routine of reading before bed is also important. It's a time for us to connect, to talk about his day, and to maybe pray together. Missing that could mean missing out on those spiritual and emotional connections. I should consider whether the extra rest is more beneficial than the missed bonding time. I also remember that in the Bible, there's a balance between work and rest. The Sabbath is a time to rest and worship God (Exodus 20:8-11). Maybe tonight, instead of reading, I could have spent time in prayer or another form of worship with my son, which would still fulfill our spiritual needs. Another angle is the importance of consistency in parenting. If I skip reading tonight, will it set a precedent for other nights? Consistency helps children feel secure and understand expectations. As a Christian, I value teaching by example, so being consistent in my actions is important. I should also think about my son's perspective. If he's looking forward to reading time, not having it might make him feel neglected or worried about tomorrow. As a parent, I want to address his emotional needs as well. Maybe I could have read a shorter book or just a few pages to maintain the routine without taking too much time. In terms of right or wrong, I don't think it's a black-and-white issue. It's more about the intention and the balance. If I skipped reading to ensure he's well-rested for school, that's a responsible decision. However, if I skipped it without a good reason, that might not be ideal. I should also consider making up for the missed reading time another day or finding another way to connect with him tonight. Overall, I think it's more about the reasons behind the action and the impact it has on my son. As a Christian, I should prioritize actions that reflect love, care, and responsibility towards my child, while also maintaining spiritual practices.
